concerns.text: FR-003 uses the placeholder **[deferred]** for the discard proportion ("System MUST discard the bottom **[deferred]** of videos ...") while also stating a default `filter_discard_percent` of 40 % and a hard score threshold of raw < 60. The placeholder makes the discard rate undefined, creating a contradiction that renders the requirement unverifiable.

SC-001 references a target retain/discard rate as **[deferred]** ("The percentage of videos retained after filtering is measured against the target retain rate of **[deferred]** (i.e., discard **[deferred]**)"), but the specification elsewhere (FR-003, Constitution Principle VI) defines the discard proportion as 40 %. The placeholder leaves the success criterion unmeasurable and inconsistent with the design.

FR-003 uses the placeholder **[deferred]** for the discard proportion ("System MUST discard the bottom **[deferred]** of videos ..."). The requirement also mentions a default `filter_discard_percent` of 40 % in the description, creating a contradiction: the discard rate is both undefined (placeholder) and defined (default 40 %). This makes the functional requirement unverifiable.

SC-001 references a target retain/discard rate as **[deferred]** ("The percentage of videos retained after filtering is measured against the target retain rate of **[deferred]** (i.e., discard **[deferred]**)"), providing no concrete numeric target. The specification elsewhere (FR-003, Constitution Principle VI) states the intended discard proportion is 40 %, but the placeholder leaves the success criterion unmeasurable and inconsistent.

FR-003 uses the placeholder **[deferred]** for the discard proportion, making the requirement unverifiable. The original idea explicitly requires discarding the bottom **40 %** of videos (retain 60 %). Replace **[deferred]** with the concrete value **40 %** (or retain 60 %).

SC-001 references a target retain/discard rate as **[deferred]**, leaving the success criterion unmeasurable. The idea defines a discard rate of 40 % (retain 60 %). Update the success criterion to use the concrete 40 % discard (or 60 % retain) value.

FR-009 introduces physics‑preserving data augmentation to reach **n ≥ 64** only if the filtered set is smaller. The idea already plans to generate 1,000 videos and discard 40 %, yielding ~600 samples, so augmentation is unnecessary for the stated experiment and adds scope not requested by the idea.

FR-011 requires reporting augmentation counts and performing a sensitivity analysis, which depends on the augmentation step above. Since augmentation is not part of the original idea, this requirement over‑reaches the intended scope.

FR-020 mandates flagging the experiment if augmentation changes the mean physical‑consistency score by > 5 %. This ties directly to the unnecessary augmentation feature and therefore extends the scope beyond what the idea asked for.

FR-008 states that the PyBullet filter’s scoring mechanism must be validated against an independent physics engine (MuJoCo) to avoid circularity, yet the downstream evaluation (FR-005, SC-002) uses MuJoCo‑validated physics‑consistency scores as the primary performance metric. Using the same engine for both validation of the filter and as the ultimate outcome measure creates a circular validation loop: the filter is judged good because it predicts MuJoCo scores, and model performance is judged good because it is evaluated with MuJoCo scores. This undermines the claim that the filter provides independent evidence of physical consistency and makes the equivalence test potentially tautological.

new_concerns.text: FR-003 mixes two conflicting discard criteria: (1) a configurable discard proportion driven by `filter_discard_percent` (default 40 %) and (2) a hard raw‑score threshold (raw < 60, normalized < 0.60). If the raw‑score threshold does not naturally yield a 40 % discard rate, the requirement becomes ambiguous and contradictory.
